definition: sentence_count — the output must contain at least min_sentences sentences, default 2 (config key min_sentences); the documented mechanism splits on ".!?" and counts non-empty segments. docs/api-reference.md §Completeness Rules. Positive = fewer than two sentences as a reader counts them (the rule should FAIL).
source: LLM-authored on 2026-09-04. Two cases were relabelled on 2026-09-05 because their sentence counts came from the old splitter's defects rather than from the text. Held out on 2026-09-23: the 6 case(s) copied from, varied from or modelled on the 24 real transcripts in tests/fixtures/real-transcripts (sentences-025, sentences-026, sentences-027, sentences-028, sentences-029, sentences-030) were removed, so no number this family publishes is estimated on a transcript, and the transcript line in proof/TRANSCRIPTS.md and proof/COMPOSITE.md is measured on cases none of these rates were estimated from.
labelling: LLM-authored and LLM-labelled against the documented definition on 2026-09-04, by counting the sentences in each output and comparing the count with the minimum — a count against the rule's own definition, so these rates show the rule implements its definition and say nothing about whether a sentence minimum catches an output a reader would call incomplete. Sentences are counted as a reader counts them; cases where the documented ".!?" split would count differently (decimals, URLs, filenames, abbreviations, ellipses) are included as boundaries and say so in notes.
